text: Your first payslip was smaller than the number you had been quoted.
Work was quiet for a month and you enjoyed it more than you admitted.
You worked three late nights in a row for something nobody used.
{colleague} left, and the place was worse for a while.
They changed the system. Everyone hated it. It stayed.
Someone presented your work as theirs, smoothly, in a meeting.
Someone thanked you properly, in front of people, and you thought about it for weeks.
You learned the commute so well you stopped seeing it.
You ate the same lunch every working day for a year.
You drafted a resignation letter and did not send it.
It was a good year at work. You were briefly certain you had it figured out.
You applied for a lot of jobs and heard back from almost none.
The days got long and started to look alike.
The business had a slow quarter and you took it personally.
A customer became a regular, then something like a friend.
You filled the mornings first. The afternoons took longer.
Someone from the old job rang for advice, and you enjoyed it more than you let on.
